feedback: This candidate changes three fields from the iteration-0 baseline, which raced 0 of 60 trials: base_speed 1.6 to 1.3, kp 3.0 to 2.5, and kd 0.15 to 0.3. The baseline evidence is clear. Every run went off track with one line-loss event and progress of 0.11 to 0.16. Max_error sat at 0.062 to 0.067 m, just above the off-track limit of 0.06 m, so the robot is losing the line on the first curves. Steering_oscillation was highest on the s-bend (0.15), which fits over-correction. The change is consistent with that evidence: lower speed gives the controller more time on tight bends, and the higher kd damps the jitter. Sensor geometry and sensor_weights are unchanged and the sign convention is unchanged, so the candidate is valid and not obviously broken. The off-track limit for body_width is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4). Because body_width cannot exceed 0.18, that limit stays at 0.06 m, so widening the body will not buy margin. Approve it so the race gives telemetry on whether speed or gain is the cause of the line loss. Before the next race, the outcome determines the next step. If it still goes off track with line_loss_events of 1 or more and max_error near 0.06, the next revision should lower base_speed further (about 1.0) and keep the gains. If it completes with small rms_error but completion_time above 3.0 s, raise base_speed toward 1.9 with kp and kd held. If it runs but steering_oscillation stays high (above about 0.1), raise kd further (about 0.5) or lower kp (about 2.0).
requested_changes: If the next race still goes off track with max_error near 0.06 and line_loss_events of 1 or more, lower base_speed to about 1.0 and keep kp 2.5 and kd 0.3, since the baseline at base_speed 1.6 was 0 of 60 finished.
If the next race completes with small rms_error but completion_time above 3.0 s, raise base_speed toward 1.9 and hold kp and kd, since the 3 s limit needs about 1.5 m/s average.
If the next race runs but steering_oscillation stays above about 0.1 on the s-bend, raise kd to about 0.5 or lower kp to about 2.0, since the s-bend baseline oscillation was 0.15.
